items.title: Eddie Alley interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 8, 2002
items.q: So he thought about it and he said, he kind of liked me and he said, “I’m going to send you to the personnel manager and you tell him the story.”

ctx.x: When I first went to the Metropolitan there was a job open on the elevator. And they said you’re going to have a job if the uniform fits you. The uniform would have fit him. It was like a sack. So I pulled it and made it fit me. And so they said well you’re never going to get off the elevator because you’re colored. I said well I needed a job. And so I took a job for about three years, whatever — my father and mother always told me whatever I do, do the best, whatever it is. Whether it’s cleaning the floor,…
Yeah. Were you, while you were doing this job, you were starting to play drums with different people?
